phases.title: Working Neutrality

trope_functions: bureaucratic recusal performed as competence
authoritative error accepted as ordinary
genre_activations.structural_function: establishes the case unit and the cost of a ruling

trope_functions: sealed testimony introduced as routine custody
genre_activations.structural_function: plants discrepancies that later justify reopening

trope_functions: impossible witness established by distance and cost
genre_activations.structural_function: fixes material limits on who can be recorded

phases.narrative_function: Establish the archive as competent, unglamorous and necessary. Forgetting should appear as the unavoidable cost of scale rather than as a policy, so the reader's first unease is diffuse and deniable.
phases.transition: A claim that procedure cannot classify without admitting a choice forces the orders into explicit justification.

phases.title: The First Claim

trope_functions: impossible witness tested against admissibility
double bookkeeping used to absorb a claim
genre_activations.structural_function: converts background absence into a live case

trope_functions: authoritative error discovered in an existing entry
genre_activations.structural_function: shows that a settled record can be contested from inside

trope_functions: redacted return staged as a claim rather than a reunion
genre_activations.structural_function: introduces the cost of absorption to a specific party

phases.narrative_function: Show that the erased can appear as a claimant and that the procedure's first instinct is to absorb rather than answer. The reader should feel the relief of a working process and the first suspicion that the process is the problem.
phases.transition: Absorption works too well; the orders formalize the standard that made absorption possible, converting precedent into policy.

phases.title: Hardening of Procedure

trope_functions: recusal formalized into a rule that decides outcomes
sealed testimony made standard practice
genre_activations.structural_function: turns forgetting from oversight into policy

trope_functions: custodian who forgets the reason for a rule
genre_activations.structural_function: exposes that the standard was authored and can be re-authored

trope_functions: copying decisions forced by scarcity of media
genre_activations.structural_function: makes drift a material consequence of policy

phases.narrative_function: Convert forgetting from accident into policy. The archive should now be visibly defending a version of itself, and the reader should recognize their own willingness to let it.
phases.transition: An external campaign against the archive supplies a threat the orders can point to instead of an argument they must make.

phases.title: Enemy Consolidation

trope_functions: necessary enemy accepted as a fact of the world
genre_activations.structural_function: supplies the external justification the orders require

trope_functions: war horizon made credible through lost copies and restricted access
genre_activations.structural_function: raises the cost ceiling without spending the war

trope_functions: double bookkeeping justified as emergency practice
genre_activations.structural_function: shows procedure bending around the threat it is said to resist

phases.narrative_function: Make deterrence seductive. The orders become the thing standing between the archive and a war over memory, and the reader should feel genuine relief at that, which is what the later vacuum will take away.
phases.transition: The threat becomes credible enough that internal disagreement about neutrality turns into a loyalty test.

phases.title: Divided Custody

trope_functions: rival readings of the same standard
sealed testimony claimed by two custodians
genre_activations.structural_function: makes the orders an object of interpretation rather than inheritance

trope_functions: inherited oath set against the claim of the excluded
genre_activations.structural_function: forces cost to be allocated between keepers, not only to claimants

trope_functions: authoritative error shown to favour one faction
genre_activations.structural_function: reveals that drift and interest can share a result

phases.narrative_function: Split the keepers over what neutrality permits. The reader should see that sincere people can defend incompatible orders, and that the dispute is about authority rather than about facts.
phases.transition: Both factions prepare for the campaign, which is also preparation for the argument they will have after it.

phases.title: Approach of War

trope_functions: necessary enemy becomes an immediate operational threat
genre_activations.structural_function: brings the horizon close without resolving it

trope_functions: oath tested by the cost of keeping it
genre_activations.structural_function: converts institutional preparation into personal obligation

trope_functions: witnesses and records cannot both be moved
genre_activations.structural_function: makes the war's cost material before it is decided

phases.narrative_function: Make the war's cost material: records moved, copies lost, witnesses who cannot travel. Victory later must have something concrete to be measured against.
phases.transition: The campaign is defeated. The orders that depended on it lose their external justification at the moment they are strongest.

phases.title: The Campaign Ends

trope_functions: victory that empties the struggle of its justification
genre_activations.structural_function: delivers the authored hinge without resolving the debt

trope_functions: triumph recorded in the same flat register as any other intake
genre_activations.structural_function: shows the institution absorbing its own victory as procedure

trope_functions: enemy removed rather than replaced
genre_activations.structural_function: forecloses the easy sequel of a larger replacement threat

phases.narrative_function: Deliver the author's fixed anchor: the Warden's long campaign ends in victory. Treat the win as a structural hinge, not a resolution: the justification disappears and the debts do not. Do not stage campaign events, tactics or aftermaths beyond the victory itself.
phases.transition: With no enemy to justify them, the orders must argue from their own record to people whose lives that record never held.

phases.title: Vacuum of Justification

trope_functions: oath defended with no threat left to point at
genre_activations.structural_function: converts external defense into internal accounting

trope_functions: recusal used to avoid answering rather than to appear fair
genre_activations.structural_function: reveals the neutrality claim as labor with no cover

trope_functions: the written justification is found to postdate the practice
genre_activations.structural_function: makes the orders historically authored in front of the reader

phases.narrative_function: Make the orders' self-justification visible as work. Every defense of neutrality should reveal a choice someone made, and the reader should feel the archive's authority thinning without collapsing.
phases.transition: The erased stop being a category the archive manages and become a party the archive must negotiate with.

phases.title: The Debt as Counterparty

trope_functions: redacted return with standing rather than restoration
genre_activations.structural_function: converts debt into negotiable claim

trope_functions: impossible witness finally admissible on changed terms
genre_activations.structural_function: shows that admissibility, not evidence, was the barrier

trope_functions: double bookkeeping produced as the price of settlement
genre_activations.structural_function: reveals that the settlement already concedes an unpaid remainder

phases.narrative_function: Convert debt into a claim with terms. What is owed cannot be settled by adding records alone, because authority over recording is the thing in dispute, and the reader should be able to name that distinction.
phases.transition: Settlement is attempted on terms the archive can survive, which means the settlement cannot be complete.

phases.title: Settlement and Residue

trope_functions: the archive's own account admits it authored its neutrality
genre_activations.structural_function: makes the series' record-keeping an explicit theme rather than a frame

trope_functions: victory that empties, now paid forward as obligation
genre_activations.structural_function: delivers a settlement with visible winners and recorded losers

trope_functions: residue entered into the record as an unpaid obligation
genre_activations.structural_function: institutionalizes the remainder instead of resolving it

phases.narrative_function: End on acknowledged residue: some obligations are recorded as unpaid, and the unease the author asked for persists knowingly rather than resolving into absolution. The reader should be able to enumerate what was settled and what was not.
phases.transition: No further transition is required. If the series continues beyond this phase, continuation must inherit the residue rather than discharge it.

open_questions: Is erasure irreversible, with records destroyed, or recoverable, with records withheld? The architecture currently assumes irreversible by default with partial reconstruction, and that assumption sets the ceiling on repair.
Is the desert archive one institution or a network of archives with rival orders? This decides whether neutrality can be local and whether the memory war is civil or external.
Are the orders a written canon or a performed tradition? This decides how amendment, schism and succession can plausibly work, and how visible the neutrality claim is to ordinary people.
Is the memory war literal, with records as war aims, or is it contested history only? This sets how much weight the memory-war epic can carry without turning the series into a war narrative.
May the series ever show an exclusion that is defensible? If every exclusion must be unjust, neutrality becomes mere hypocrisy; if some are defensible, the intended unease becomes genuinely tragic.
Does the Warden remain a party after the Book 26 victory? The architecture currently assumes the victory removes the enemy role rather than recycling the same antagonist as a later threat.
Are keepers beneficiaries of the orders or captive servants of them? This changes whose complicity the reader is asked to share, and whether reform costs the keepers status or safety.
May the erased speak through specific representatives, or must the claim stay collective? The architecture keeps it collective at first and does not decide whether it narrows to a named party later.
May the ending leave debt unpaid? The architecture proposes acknowledged residue; the author may require actual discharge, which would change the final phase's whole payoff logic.

Does the forty-Book horizon permit generational time jumps? The relay structure assumes it does; if not, succession must compress into one keeper's lifetime and the recurrence rate of the case unit changes.
May the reader ever be given a record that is definitively true? If yes, unease can resolve into judgment; if no, the series risks relativism and must work harder to keep accountability traceable.
Is the Book 26 victory military, political or evidentiary? The architecture treats it abstractly, but the mechanism determines what the justification vacuum can actually do in the following phases.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader dreads the archive's verdict as a threat that could fall on anyone, including themselves, and learns to fear classification rather than violence.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: A routine adjudication in which a life's admissibility turns on a procedural detail nobody can supply, such as a missing witness, an inadmissible language, or an unverified copy.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Documentary dryness with clinical detail: the flatness makes the threat feel administrative, so fear attaches to paperwork instead of to a threatening figure.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader is repelled by the machinery of impartiality itself, not by a villain, and begins to hear the word neutral as a claim rather than a description.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: A scrupulously fair procedure produces an outcome that is visibly unjust while every participant behaves correctly and can defend their conduct.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Understated revelation and managed absence: the reader is shown the clean surface and the gap it conceals, so revulsion comes from noticing rather than from being told.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader grieves lives that never became records, and the grief accumulates across the series instead of being discharged by any single loss.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: Repeated encounters with absence that has left a trace: a catalogue number without a record, a name in a margin, a copy that exists only as a reference.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Material motifs of drift and burial give grief a physical grammar, so it attaches to sand, fading and travel rather than to invented biography.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader wants to hold the orders accountable as an authored arrangement, not as an unfortunate inheritance, and directs anger at justification rather than at fate.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: A defense of neutrality that reveals a choice someone made and benefited from, delivered in the register of inevitability.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Documentary dryness exposes the gap between the calm wording of a rule and the cost it allocates, letting anger arrive through comparison rather than accusation.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader is startled to discover that the archive's neutrality was decided rather than found, and re-reads earlier competence as construction.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: A revelation that a foundational practice has a date, an author, or a dispute behind it, disclosed as a clerical or custodial detail.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Understated revelation: the disclosure arrives as a correction in a record the reader already trusts, so surprise comes from reinterpreting what was already seen.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader feels the genuine relief and joy of being recorded, which makes the archive's power desirable and prevents the series from becoming a one-note indictment.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: A claimant is admitted, a name is entered, or a life becomes legible to an institution that will now protect it in some small way.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Restraint releases briefly: a plain sentence, a completed form, an unremarkable entry given weight by the surrounding dryness.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader takes pleasure in an order that works and prevents a war, so that the later accounting costs them something they actually valued.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: A moment when the archive's procedure visibly averts escalation, protects a record from seizure, or keeps a dispute inside argument rather than force.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Vastness and enclosure make the archive feel like shelter, and procedural competence is staged as genuinely satisfying craft.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader fears the war over memory enough to accept the orders as a lesser evil, and notices later that this fear was also an argument used against claimants.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: Evidence of what a memory war costs: records seized, copies destroyed, access refused, witnesses stranded, and disputes that leave argument for force.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Multi-register testimony shows the same loss in official, personal and hostile accounts, so the threat feels documented rather than declared.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader feels the specific sadness of successors who must answer for losses they did not cause and cannot fully repair.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: A keeper inherits a standard, an oath, or an unresolved claim and discovers what it cost someone who is no longer present to be asked.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Vastness and enclosure stage the keeper alone with a record that outlasts the person who made it, letting scale carry the sadness.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader feels sharp anger when a sworn standard is exposed as a convenience, and registers that the betrayal is institutional rather than personal.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: A keeper's oath is shown to have been written, amended or waived in a way that served the institution's authority while claiming continuity.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Documentary dryness lets the betrayal appear as a version difference between two texts rather than as a confrontation.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader fears what happens to an institution that has won and lost its reason, and expects the accounting to be worse than the war.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: After the campaign's victory, the orders must justify themselves with no external threat available, and the first attempts sound hollow to the people hearing them.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Managed absence does the work: the missing enemy is felt as a structural hole in every justification that follows.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader is surprised by a record turning out otherwise than its authority implied, and learns to read every confident entry as provisional.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: A sealed, authoritative or inherited record is shown to contain a different account than the one the archive has been acting on.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Multi-register testimony stages the competing accounts side by side, so the surprise is produced by juxtaposition rather than by a twist.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader grieves the limit of repair, accepting that a settlement can be real and still insufficient, which is the emotional honesty the premise requires.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: A settlement is reached that restores standing to some claimants while explicitly recording others as permanently unpaid.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Managed absence and documentary dryness let the remainder be stated plainly in the record, so sadness comes from the entry rather than from commentary.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader feels real relief at a partial settlement, so the series can end with something gained rather than only with loss acknowledged.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: A claim that was previously inadmissible becomes admissible, and a specific obligation is formally accepted by the institution that denied it.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Restraint breaks once: a plain procedural sentence carries the weight, and the dryness around it makes the concession feel earned.

emotion_targets.intended_effect: The reader fears the position of the decider, recognizing that anyone who rules will produce exclusion, which converts sympathy for keepers into discomfort.
emotion_targets.eliciting_condition: A keeper must rule on a case where every available decision violates something the keeper believes, and deferral is itself a ruling.
emotion_targets.aesthetic_strategy: Understated revelation keeps the moment quiet: the reader watches a hand complete a form rather than a figure make a speech.

complex_emotions.title: Governing Unease
complex_emotions.context: The compound the author names as unease: fear that the archive's verdict could fall on anyone, disgust that impartial machinery produces it, and sadness for the lives it has already cost. Interpreted here as a reading posture rather than a clinical state, and it is strongest when the reader cannot locate a single party to blame.

complex_emotions.title: Complicity
complex_emotions.context: Pleasure at an institution that spares the reader from deciding, curdling into revulsion when the reader notices the cost of that relief. The joy is real, which is why the disgust has somewhere to come from; this is the hinge emotion between early comfort and late reckoning.

complex_emotions.title: Institutional Faith
complex_emotions.context: Trust in an order that is sustained by the threat it guards against, so that reassurance and dread arrive together. Interpreted as the emotional signature of deterrence rather than as a claim about how belief works.

complex_emotions.title: Archival Grief
complex_emotions.context: Grief that refuses consolation because it has become a demand for accounting. It differs from ordinary loss by attaching to a procedure rather than to a person, and it is the emotional form the erased counterclaim takes when it acquires standing.

complex_emotions.title: Vindication Emptiness
complex_emotions.context: The shape of the Book 26 victory: a long campaign is won and the win removes the condition that made the struggle coherent. Joy belongs to the winners and is not fake; sadness belongs to what the win reveals about why the orders were obeyed.

complex_emotions.title: Bureaucratic Revulsion
complex_emotions.context: Revulsion produced by a banal administrative detail that suddenly reveals how the machinery works. Surprise is essential: the detail must be something the reader has already seen many times without registering its implication.

complex_emotions.title: Inherited Shame
complex_emotions.context: A successor's relation to orders they did not author but continue to enforce: disgust at the arrangement, sadness for what it cost, fear of what disowning it would cost them. It is not guilt about intention, since the keeper may have intended nothing.

complex_emotions.title: Reckoning Dread
complex_emotions.context: The compound of approaching an obligation that cannot be discharged by apology or by addition: fear of the terms, anger at having inherited them, and surprise at how much of the debt turns out to be about authority rather than information.

trope_functions: bureaucratic recusal as the visible ritual of impartiality
sealed testimony as the withheld stake of a case
authoritative error as the consequence of ordinary practice
genre_contracts.narrative_engine: record adjudication, exercised through a renewable case unit with rotating case classes and one contested criterion per case
genre_contracts.structural_pattern: recursive case unit escalating into debt escalation, with nested reopening when standards change
genre_contracts.payoff_expectations: Every case must deliver a ruling whose criterion the reader can inspect and dispute. Refusals must cost someone standing rather than spectacle, and no ruling may be correct in a way that resolves the underlying argument.

trope_functions: necessary enemy as the prop of legitimacy
victory that empties the struggle
inherited oath as obligation without authorship
genre_contracts.narrative_engine: neutrality fabrication under pressure, converting every defense of order into an allocation of cost
genre_contracts.structural_pattern: debt escalation culminating in a hinge that changes justification instead of clearing obligation
genre_contracts.payoff_expectations: Cost must land on identifiable parties, including keepers. The Book 26 victory must be shown as a reallocation of justification rather than a release, and no settlement may return anyone to their prior standing.

trope_functions: sealed testimony reopened on changed authority
impossible witness whose failure exposes the standard
redacted return as a claim with standing
genre_contracts.narrative_engine: testimony conversion and record drift, producing discrepancies that force standards to be re-argued
genre_contracts.structural_pattern: nested reopening with cascading precedent, bounded by institutional willingness to re-examine
genre_contracts.payoff_expectations: Inquiry must change what a record means or who bears the burden, never merely add a fact. Each discovery must be traceable to a custody, copying or classification decision that someone made for a reason.

trope_functions: authoritative error as an epistemic condition
custodian who forgets the ground of a rule
double bookkeeping as an official admission
genre_contracts.narrative_engine: record drift and neutrality fabrication, keeping the question of authorship attached to every record
genre_contracts.structural_pattern: nested reopening paired with the double ledger, ending in explicit admission of authorship
genre_contracts.payoff_expectations: The series must eventually show that the archive's neutrality was authored, and must trace the claim to a decision, an office and a beneficiary. Authorship must never diffuse into the claim that no one is responsible.

trope_functions: impossible witness created by distance and water
redacted return carried by migration rather than by reunion
genre_contracts.narrative_engine: desert scarcity and record drift, pricing every act of remembering
genre_contracts.structural_pattern: generational relay paced by drought, migration and media decay rather than by years
genre_contracts.payoff_expectations: Material cost must constrain who can make claims, and scarcity must never be mere scenery. Every movement of records or witnesses must cost something that could otherwise have preserved a life.

trope_functions: necessary enemy held at horizon scale
victory that empties rather than replaces the threat
genre_contracts.narrative_engine: memory-war deterrence and enemy dependence, with the war as a pressure reading rather than a promised confrontation
genre_contracts.structural_pattern: distributed climax with a hinge that forecloses a replacement enemy
genre_contracts.payoff_expectations: The war must remain a horizon the series refuses to spend cheaply. If it becomes actual, it must arrive as the consequence of a failed settlement, and its cost must be measured in lost records, lost access and stranded witnesses rather than in battle spectacle.

genre_interactions.mechanism: Case form stages the question of what a record can know as a procedural question with a ruling attached, so epistemology acquires stakes and a deadline.
genre_interactions.risk: Procedural closure can flatten genuine ambiguity into a solved case, making the archive look merely under-informed rather than constitutive.

genre_interactions.mechanism: Tragedy forbids costless rulings, so every procedure must allocate loss to an identifiable party and cannot resolve a case by finding the right form.
genre_interactions.risk: Relentless cost can make the institution merely villainous and destroy the relief that the architecture needs in order to produce complicity.

genre_interactions.mechanism: Inquiry supplies the discrepancies, provenance questions and competing copies that give each case something to argue about beyond its own paperwork.
genre_interactions.risk: Inquiry can become the only plot and reduce institutional pressure to puzzle-solving, at which point the archive stops being the subject.

genre_interactions.mechanism: Travel, water and heat ration who can appear as a witness and what evidence can be carried, so discovery is limited by logistics rather than by ingenuity.
genre_interactions.risk: Logistics can dominate and stall inquiry rhythm, turning structural pressure into an itinerary.

genre_interactions.mechanism: Epic scale demands stakes beyond a single case, while procedure demands jurisdiction, so every attempt to raise stakes threatens the frame that makes the series arguable.
genre_interactions.risk: The war horizon can swallow local stakes or remain an empty threat, either of which weakens the deterrence engine.

genre_interactions.mechanism: If records are authored, accountability diffuses; tragedy needs someone who can answer for the cost, so the two genres pull the series in opposite directions.
genre_interactions.risk: Relativism that dissolves the intended unease into the claim that no one is responsible, which contradicts the author's commitment that neutrality is a justification rather than a fact.

genre_interactions.mechanism: Both convert the past into a claim on the present, so the campaign's end can serve as a shared event: a victory for one register and an indictment in the other.
genre_interactions.risk: Convergence can make the war feel like the tragedy's only available climax and pull the series toward spectacle.

genre_interactions.mechanism: Scarcity of durable copies makes records worth seizing and worth defending, which is what gives a war over memory a material object.
genre_interactions.risk: Material logic can imply the war is only about supply, reducing a conflict over authority to a conflict over stock.

genre_interactions.mechanism: Procedure is the dam: war stays a horizon while adjudication still works, so escalation is measured by procedural failure rather than by declarations.
genre_interactions.risk: Over-constraint can mean the promised war never arrives, which erodes the credibility the deterrence engine depends on.

genre_interactions.mechanism: Discoveries become the reversals tragedy spends, because a changed record changes who bears the cost without changing the institution that allocated it.
genre_interactions.risk: Too many reversals can make the orders look incompetent rather than interested in forgetting, which weakens the systemic argument.
